title: No FSD module exists for the platform, so no FSD requirement ID states a platform capability
source: Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 (19 module files); PRD Builder work package B-REQ-PRD-PLT
section: 1.1 Document control; 1.4 Requirement ID conventions; 6 Functional requirements; Appendix A.2
description: The FSD v6 set carries one file per module P1-P10 and S1-S9 and none for the platform. A platform functional requirement therefore has no FSD requirement ID of its own: it names the FSD requirement of the module whose behaviour depends on the mechanism, and the BRD non-functional requirement that sets its target.
evidence: The zip of Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6 lists 19 .md files and no PLT file; _work/msr/extract/ holds the same 19 files.
legacy_ref: N001 to N012; NF-01 to NF-08
proposed: Write the platform functional specification as the T0 Service section of the Technical Specifications by Module v6, or as a PLT module file, and map FR-PLT-001 to FR-PLT-034 to its requirement IDs.

title: No predecessor PRD exists in the PLT family
description: The PRD folder holds P1-P10 and S1-S6 files and no PLT file, so this document is version 1 rather than a next version of an existing PRD.
evidence: The PRD folder listing shows Recovery Workbench PRD P1 to P10 and S1 to S6 v1 files and no PLT file.
proposed: Treat this file as the family baseline v1 and version from it.

title: The retry limit of an event and of a call is stated differently in the BRD and in Architecture v5
source: BRD Program v5 NFR-026; Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slides 26 and 28
description: BRD NFR-026 says three retries per item and then the exception queue. Architecture v5 slide 11 sets retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and then a dead-letter topic with an alert, and the Temporal design sets an activity retry policy of 1 s initial interval, doubling, up to 10 attempts. The three statements describe three different paths, not one.
evidence: BRD Program v5 NFR-026 text; Arch v5 slide 11 (Timeout, retry row); Temporal and Drools Design slide 28 notes (retry policy 1 s, back-off 2, 10 attempts).
proposed: Publish one retry table: three retries per outbound item to the exception queue (P2), retry topics 1/10/60 min then .dlt with an alert for events, and 10 activity attempts with a non-retryable list for Temporal.

title: The feature-flag store has an owner and a schema in the Ownership Map but no service row
source: Ownership Map v1 (Tables, Endpoints, Services sheets); Ownership Map ruling ASM-A6-tables-7 and ASM-A6-api-2
description: The Ownership Map gives feature_flag and feature_flag_change the owner PLT and the schema platform, and gives the four feature-flag paths the owner PLT, while the Services sheet has 19 rows and no platform row. The ruling says P2 serves the four paths against the library. Where the two flag tables physically live, and which component answers a flag read, is therefore not stated.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables sheet: feature_flag, feature_flag_change owner PLT, schema 'platform'; Services sheet: 19 rows, no platform row; Endpoints sheet: GET /feature-flags, GET /admin/feature-flags, POST /admin/feature-flags, PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey} owner PLT.
proposed: Name the platform store and the component that serves the four paths, and add the missing platform row to the service catalogue if the store is a deployable.

title: The environment set, its names and its sizing are not stated
source: Environment and Deployment Design v5 (per-service deployments; environment names recorded as a gap); Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 33 and 39
description: Architecture v5 names DEV, SIT, UAT and production in passing and sets no count, no name pattern and no size per environment. The document family records the environment names as a gap, so the template cannot be parameterised from a source.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 39 (connection budget per service); _work/msr/plan/docs.json note for the Environment and Deployment Design v5: 'per-service deployments; environment names are a gap'.
proposed: Agree four environments (development, system integration, user acceptance, production) with one name pattern and one size table before wave 0 starts.

title: The repository and pipeline product is not named in any source
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 33 and 38; Story Template and Rules v1 R8.3
description: Architecture v5 requires one Helm chart, one golden pipeline and one pipeline template per service and names no product. No source names the repository host, the pipeline tool or the artefact registry, so the pipeline requirement is stated as an outcome only.
evidence: Arch v5 slides 33 and 38 name 'one Helm chart', 'golden pipeline' and 'one pipeline template' with no product name.
proposed: Name the repository, pipeline and registry products and record them in the Environment and Deployment Design v5.

title: Several platform targets are unset: recovery point and time, the per-namespace quotas, the key rotation period and the retention periods
source: BRD Program v5 NFR-022, NFR-023, NFR-030 and section 9 DL11 and DL26; Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 39
description: NFR-022 and NFR-023 are open under DL11 and are answered as 'the ACE values'. The Temporal namespace needs quotas, rate limits and a key rotation period that no source states; the retention of the platform rows and the telemetry is open under DL26.
evidence: BRD Program v5 NFR-022 and NFR-023 status 'Open, DL11'; NFR-030 status 'Open, DL26'; the namespace decision on Arch v5 slide 39 names retention and quotas as the platform's own values.
proposed: Set the targets under DL11 and DL26 before the wave-1 release and record them in the Non Functional Specification v4.

title: The BRD carries no approval record and no status field
source: BRD Program v5; BRD Epic 1 v5; BRD Epic 2 v3; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1
description: No BRD version in the source set carries a status field, an approval table with a decision, or a signature. The requirements approval gate therefore cannot be evidenced from the baseline, and this PRD is issued as Draft.
evidence: Document control tables of the four BRDs carry title, identifier, version, status 'In review' or none, classification and date, and no approval row with a decision.
proposed: Record the Product Owner and FDA decision on the BRD and on this PRD at the requirements approval gate.

title: The owner of record for the shared Temporal cluster and for the Kafka hosting is not named
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 39 (decisions 1 and 3); slide 2 ('owner for the shared Temporal layer')
description: Architecture v5 asks for a decision on hosting Recovery's business-event topics on the bank Kafka platform or the Event Hubs fallback, and on a shared Temporal layer owned by the platform team, and records both with an owner group and no single accountable team. An outage of either stops every running journey, and no requirement can be accepted against an unnamed owner.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 39 rows 1 and 3; slide 2 'What we need from you: owner for the shared Temporal layer'.
proposed: Name the accountable team for the cluster and for the topics, and record both in the Service Catalog v1.

title: The Airflow ownership, its placement and the date Control-M moves are open
source: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 ('To agree'); slides 31 and 44
description: Airflow is described as a recommendation to discuss: who owns the DAGs, where Airflow runs, when Control-M moves and whether a new ADR replaces the BRD's ADF and Control-M wording are all listed as open. The platform therefore states the edge contract and not the scheduler's owner.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 32 notes: 'To agree: who owns the DAGs (bank platform team or Recovery), when Control-M moves to Airflow, where Airflow runs, and a new ADR replacing the BRD's ADF/Control-M wording.'
proposed: Record the Airflow decision in a new ADR and name the DAG owner before the wave-1 release.

title: The retention of the platform rows, of the stored idempotent answer and of the telemetry is not stated
source: BRD Program v5 NFR-030 and section 9 DL26; Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11
description: No source states how long an outbox row, an inbox row, an idempotency record, a flag change row, a telemetry signal or a workflow history beyond the 30-day closed-history rule is kept. The idempotency answer period is not stated either.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 11 names the Idempotency-Key and the stored response with no period; BRD NFR-030 is 'Open, DL26'.
proposed: Set the retention per platform object under DL26 and record it in the Logical Data Model next version.

title: The masking and scrubbing list for telemetry is not stated
source: BRD Program v5 NFR-039 and NFR-040; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35
description: The sources require that personal data stays in the owning service and that no personal data appears in a log, an event or a workflow payload, and they do not state which fields are masked or scrubbed, per role or per signal. A telemetry scrubbing rule with no field list cannot be tested.
evidence: BRD Program v5 NFR-039 and NFR-040; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012 ('what are the retention periods and the masking rules, by record class and by role'); Arch v5 slide 35 notes on PDPA.
proposed: Publish the masked and scrubbed field list per role, and apply it to the telemetry pipeline and the prompt path.

title: The partner gateway provision and its penetration-test scope are open
source: Non Functional Specification v3 section 4 and section 5 ('Partners: Open, DL03'); Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35
description: The sources place the partner gateway in the DMZ under FAPI 2.0 and leave partner access open under DL03. They do not state whether the bank platform provides the gateway or the programme builds it, and they set no scope for the penetration test that must pass before it opens.
evidence: Non Functional Specification v3 section 1 ('Partners: Partner access from outside the bank through the external gateway - Open, DL03'); Arch v5 slide 35 notes (partners: separate DMZ gateway; penetration test before launch).
proposed: Decide the provision under DL03 and agree the penetration-test scope before the first partner release.
